name: publicWeb_redeemAdminToken
description: Validates and redeems a one-time admin token generated by hcportal_generateWebAdminToken. Called by the Next.js /api/admin/auth route (through PublicWebAdminApi, exempt from HC_INTERNAL_SECRET — this is the public OTP step) to exchange the URL token for a session cookie. Tokens expire 10 minutes after issue and are deleted on first use by a single atomic DELETE … OUTPUT, so two concurrent redemptions cannot both succeed (H14 fix). Zero rows means invalid, expired, already used, or an error; the caller returns 401. Since 2026-10-13 its CATCH logs to HC.ErrorLog before returning no rows (it swallowed the error silently).

parameters.name: Token
parameters.description: UUID token string from the URL ?token= parameter. NULL or empty returns no rowset at all (RETURN before the SELECT).
parameters.typeMismatch: PublicWebAdminToken.Id is UNIQUEIDENTIFIER; the SP takes NVARCHAR(36) and compares LOWER(CAST(Id AS NVARCHAR(36))) = LOWER(@Token), which cannot use the primary key index.

rowsets.name: RedemptionResult
rowsets.description: Zero rows = invalid, expired or already-used token, or a runtime error (the CATCH returns nothing). One row = valid token, now deleted. When @Token is NULL/empty no result set is returned at all.

columns.name: KennelSlug
columns.description: The kennel slug the token was issued for — caller verifies this matches the URL slug before creating the session cookie

sideEffects: DELETE the redeemed row from HC.PublicWebAdminToken (one-time use), atomically with reading its KennelSlug.

codeSmells.detail: Line 37 casts and lower-cases every Id to compare with the string, scanning HC.PublicWebAdminToken instead of seeking the primary key. TRY_CAST(@Token AS UNIQUEIDENTIFIER) = Id would seek. The table is tiny (rows live 10 minutes), so the cost is negligible today.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove the KennelSlug column — the Next.js route uses it to verify the token's kennel matches the URL
Never change zero-rows = invalid to an error envelope — the caller specifically checks rowset length
Never make the token multi-use — the DELETE must always happen on a valid redemption
